# aibris v0.8.1

This reliability patch makes cleanup evidence easier to understand and harder
to misuse. It focuses on fail-closed agent-state classification, one physical
cleanup plan across overlapping discoveries, and stronger scan-to-delete
revalidation.

## Highlights

- Claude and Cursor project stores now use recorded working directories to
  classify entries as `live`, `orphaned`, or `undetermined`. Only proven
  orphaned state is eligible by default.
- Mixed guided and classic cleanup shares one physical-owner plan. Nested
  evidence remains visible while projected and reclaimed bytes are counted
  once.
- Cached cleanup targets are revalidated for identity, type, age, and
  modification time before selection and immediately before mutation.
- Partial provider scans cannot authorize cleanup, and guided review continues
  into classic candidates rather than hiding them.
- Worktree discovery covers registered Codex, Relay, GStack, and Superpowers
  containers while retaining bounded convention discovery.
- CLI help and warnings now use the same selected/reviewable/protected/locked
  vocabulary as the enforced policy.

## Safety

- Live, ambiguous, newly changed, or overlapping agent state protects its whole
  physical cleanup component.
- Missing agent-state revalidators are a hard refusal for that item.
- Recorded-cwd filesystem boundaries fail closed on Unix and Windows. Windows
  uses `GetVolumePathNameW`; lookup failure remains `undetermined`.
- Compiled CLI contracts cover destructive isolation, prompts, signals, exit
  status, and Windows executable naming.

## Windows status

Windows archives remain experimental. Native CI covers recorded-cwd safety,
platform-safe command behavior, build, and vet. Download the matching
`aibris_windows_*.zip`, verify it against `checksums.txt`, and place
`aibris.exe` on `PATH`; the Bash installer is not a native Windows installer.

See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/sungjunlee/aibris/blob/v0.8.1/CHANGELOG.md)
for the complete curated change list.
